description: Sign-in required: call connect(email) and connect_verify first (free, one email) unless this connection is already signed in. What one document or article relies on (cituoja): the acts (įstatymai) and earlier rulings (nutartys) it cites, each with its pinpoint, court and date and the citing sentence so you can check it. Use it to follow a ruling's reasoning back to its sources; for the reverse direction (which later rulings cite this act, article or ruling) use cited_by. It lists citations, not agreement: whether the court followed or distinguished a source is not determined, so read the passage with read_paragraphs. The set is a slice: check `provisions_total` before concluding a source is absent. Pass the search hit `id`: an article id (with `#`) asks about that article, a document id about the whole document. Example arguments: {"document_id": "<document_id or article id from a result>", "limit": 10}.

detail.description: `compact` (the default) keeps each edge's identity, pinpoint, court and date whole and cuts `quote` (the citing sentence) to ~300 characters, with `quote_chars` giving its full length. `full` returns every quote whole.
detail.title: Detail

document_id.description: Whose citations to list. An ARTICLE id (the search hit `id`, containing `#`) asks what that article relies on; a document id asks about the whole document. There is no `pinpoint` parameter - the article is named by the id.
document_id.title: Document Id

jurisdiction.description: Which jurisdiction the id belongs to, as a code. Held: `LT` (Lithuania), `EU` (European Union). Omit for the account's own.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

limit.description: How many edges to return, default 25. Read `provisions_total` beside the answer before concluding something is absent: the returned set is a slice, not the population.
limit.title: Limit

max_chars.description: A hard cap on the answer's size in characters, default 15000. Every row is first narrowed (a ~150-character excerpt), then rows are dropped from the end (the lowest-ranked) to fit, and `truncated` says how many and how to get them; data_as_of, notes and caveats are never cut.
max_chars.title: Max Chars

session.description: The `session` value the sign-in returned. Pass it on every call in this conversation, so the sign-in survives however this client handles connections; omit it when the user connected with Sign in (OAuth) or a key.

name: citations_of
title: What this document cites
